Fetch the OSM access network (roads + trails) for a domain

Source: R/fn_download.R
osm_access.Rd

A convenience fetcher for the A (accessibility) and C (complementarity) terms: pulls the OpenStreetMap highway network inside a bounding box from an Overpass endpoint and returns it as sf lines, ready to pass as sources to cost_distance. OpenTrailMap and similar viewers are just renderers of this same OSM data.

Usage

osm_access(
  bbox,
  crs = NULL,
  roads = c("motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary", "tertiary", "unclassified",
    "residential", "service", "living_street", "road"),
  trails = c("path", "footway", "track", "bridleway", "cycleway", "steps"),
  path = NULL,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  endpoint = "https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter",
  contact = NULL,
  tiles = 1L,
  exclude = NULL,
  pause = 1,
  max_tries = 4L,
  timeout = 50
)

Arguments

bbox

the domain: an sf/terra object (its extent is used), or a numeric c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in lon/lat (EPSG:4326).

crs

output CRS (anything sf::st_crs accepts). Defaults to the input object's CRS, else lon/lat.

roads, trails

OSM highway values to treat as each class; the returned lines carry a class column ("road"/"trail"). Set either to character(0) to skip it.

path

file to write the merged network to (GeoPackage). NULL (default) writes osm_access.gpkg in the working directory.

cache_dir

directory for per-tile checkpoints (one .rds per tile). NULL (default) uses a folder named after path beside it. Existing tiles here are reused unless overwrite = TRUE; delete it to force a fresh pull.

overwrite

refetch and overwrite cached tiles (default FALSE).

endpoint

Overpass API URL (default the public instance - override for your own).

contact

optional contact string appended to the User-Agent (opt-in; e.g. a project URL or email you choose to share). NULL sends none.

tiles

split the bbox into a tiles x tiles grid of requests (default 1).

exclude

optional geometry (sf/sfc, any CRS) of ground already covered elsewhere; any tile falling entirely within it is skipped - never fetched - so overlapping pulls don't re-query the API. Its benefit grows as tiles shrink toward the excluded regions' size.

pause

minimum seconds between requests (default 1); also the base of the retry backoff.

max_tries

attempts per tile before giving up (default 4).

timeout

Overpass server-side [timeout:] seconds (default 50).

Value

an sf object of LINESTRINGs with osm_id, highway and class columns, in crs; attributes timestamp (OSM base time) and path (where it was written). Pass straight to cost_distance as sources.

Details

Be a good citizen. Public Overpass instances are a shared, volunteer-run resource with a tight usage policy. This helper makes only modest promises and tries to behave:

  • Batches a large domain into tiles^2 smaller queries rather than one giant one.

  • Checkpoints every tile to cache_dir the moment it returns, and on a re-run skips any tile already cached - so an interrupted or retried pull resumes instead of re-hammering the API.

  • Breathes between calls (req_throttle) and backs off exponentially on transient failures / rate limits (429/502/503/504, honouring any Retry-After).

  • Sends a plain User-Agent and never your identity. If you have a contact address you are willing to share per OSM etiquette, pass it in contact - it is opt-in, never read from your session.

For anything heavy, run your own Overpass instance (or a provider you have an account with) and point endpoint at it - do not hammer the public API.

Data is \(\copyright\) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL: attribute it, and snapshot the result (the timestamp attribute records the OSM base time) so analyses stay reproducible as OSM changes.
